subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but either direction changes permission-sensitive routing semantics across session state, auth/provider choice, and Discord delivery behavior.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord account IDs to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct matchedBy diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime routing unchanged and improve doctor/status/docs warnings for Discord accounts that appear intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair or replace the fork PR
options.body: Use the open fork PR as source material only after resolving conflicts, adding the configured-agent guard, and supplying real Discord proof.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord account IDs to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct matchedBy diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sits on the shared multi-agent routing contract and Discord helper boundary where steipete has the strongest history signal.
